page: Amazon Web Services m9g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. It features 64 dedicated physical cores based on the ARMv9 architecture, specifically the Neoverse-V3 model, running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU stress tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and static web serving throughput. Memory performance is highly competitive, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching top-tier levels and large block read/write operations demonstrating strong throughput. Database operations, particularly Redis SET operations, also register in the top tier. However, single-core CPU performance is average, and LLM text generation speeds for small models are relatively low, with text generation for a 135M model falling into the bottom tier.

Given its dedicated ARMv9 core architecture and high resource density, the m9g.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage ARM64 architecture. The absence of local storage means workloads rely entirely on network-attached storage. This instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, high-throughput static web serving, and data compression tasks, while being less optimal for workloads requiring high single-core performance or local SSD storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m9g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 64 dedicated physical cores at 3.3 GHz and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB per core ratio. The instance lacks local storage and GPUs but provides a baseline network bandwidth of 34 Gbps. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and Redis database operations. Conversely, single-core performance is average, and small-model LLM text generation is poor. This profile makes the m9g.16xlarge qualitatively cost-efficient for highly parallelized, memory-intensive ARM64 workloads. It is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, database management, and multi-threaded data processing, though it requires network-attached storage for persistent data.
